correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md proof reconstructs correctly. For an arbitrary centered ellipse E_Q inside the cut-square octagon, the four strip support inequalities give tr(Q)<=2 min{1,(1+w)^2/2}. Averaging v v^T over the eight vertices gives ((1+w^2)/2)I, so K_w subset lambda E_Q implies lambda^2 >= (1+w^2) tr(Q^{-1})/2 >= (1+w^2)/q_* by tr(Q^{-1})>=4/tr(Q). The circle sqrt(q_*) B_2 attains equality. The two branches meet at w=sqrt(2)-1 and their derivatives give the claimed unique minimum.

originality.rationale: The exact numeric formula is not printed in the exact-object papers inspected, but the final claim is implication-level covered by a stronger 2026 planar distance-ellipsoid theorem plus routine symmetry and radial geometry. Grundbacher's Corollary 2.11 proves uniqueness of the distance-ellipsoid pair for every planar symmetric convex body. Because K_w has the full signed-permutation symmetry, uniqueness forces its distance ellipse to be a Euclidean circle. The Banach–Mazur distance is then only the ratio of the octagon's Euclidean circumradius to its Euclidean inradius, whose two strip families immediately give exactly the submitted two branches and the junction w=sqrt(2)-1. Under the required corollary/special-case standard, absence of the same displayed formula is not originality.
